name: IBM Bob
description: AI-first development partner for enterprise teams that works across the full software development lifecycle (SDLC), from planning and coding to testing, deployment, and modernization. Features multi-model orchestration (dynamically routes tasks to Claude, Mistral, Granite, and specialized fine-tuned models), intelligent modernization, security controls built-in, and auditability with self-documenting processes.
community_quotes: Developers surveyed reported an average 70% reduction in time spent on selected tasks, equaling an average time savings of 10 hours per week
Bob helped conduct a typical 30-day Java upgrade in just 3 days, saving over 160 engineering hours
Bob migrated complex .NET services in hours instead of weeks
80,000+ IBM employees currently using IBM Bob; surveyed users report average 45% productivity gain

name: Gas City
description: Orchestration-builder SDK for multi-agent coding workflows. A ground-up rewrite of Gas Town as a composable SDK for building and deploying autonomous agent 'dark factories' with arbitrary topologies. Features declarative city configuration (city.toml), Beads-backed work tracking (MEOW stack), multiple runtime providers (tmux, subprocess, exec, ACP, Kubernetes), controller/supervisor loop, complete Git/Dolt-based audit trails, and Factory Worker API for coding agent maintainers.
community_quotes: Gas City launched on April 24 (UTC+8), repositioned as a general-purpose orchestrator from its predecessor Gas Town
Should you switch from Gas Town to Gas City? Yes! Gas City aims to be better in every way
Small team of three to five human engineers running Gas City packs can credibly replace seven-figure SaaS bills
Gas City is completely open-sourced and MIT-licensed. Built for enterprise, fun for tinkerers
